=={{header|Cxc}}==

Lists are FP, so the shuffle is reshaped: each step picks a random index from the remaining pool, moves that element to the result, drops it from the pool, and repeats. `Random` is an explicit capability on the atom.

<syntaxhighlight lang="elixir">
def main:
    use console: Console
    use random: Random

    pool: List of Int! = []
    result: List of Int! = []

    -> seeding
        self :> seed(1)

    seeding <: seed(i: Int):
        |:  i > 10 -> shuffling
            self :> step
        |?: -> seeding
            pool => self.pool.append(i)
            self :> seed(i + 1)

    shuffling <: step:
        |:  self.pool.count() == 0 -> printing
            self :> show(0)
        |?: -> shuffling
            let j: Int! = random.below(self.pool.count()) ?? 0
            let picked: Int! = self.pool.at(j) ?? 0
            result => self.result.append(picked)
            pool => self.pool.filter(x => x != picked)
            self :> step

    printing <: show(i: Int):
        |:  i >= self.result.count() -> end
        |?: -> printing
            console.write((self.result.at(i) ?? 0).to_string())
            self :> show(i + 1)
</syntaxhighlight>
